name: California SB 53: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
summary: California law on frontier models (trained above 10^26 operations). All frontier developers must publish transparency reports when deploying new or substantially modified frontier models, report critical safety incidents, and observe whistleblower protections. Large frontier developers (over $500 million annual gross revenue) must also publish a frontier AI framework, send internal-use catastrophic risk summaries to the Office of Emergency Services, and provide an anonymous internal reporting process. Enforced by the Attorney General. Effective 1 January 2026 under the California Constitution's default rule for non-urgency statutes; the CalCompute provisions become operative only upon a budget appropriation.
key_obligations: Large frontier developers: publish a frontier AI framework, review it at least once per year and update as appropriate; publish material modifications with a justification within 30 days
Frontier developers: publish a transparency report before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model

Frontier developers: report critical safety incidents to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovery; if an incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, disclose it within 24 hours to an appropriate authority (e.g. law enforcement or a public safety agency)
Large frontier developers: send OES summaries of catastrophic risk assessments from internal use every three months or on another reasonable schedule communicated to OES in writing
Whistleblower protections for covered employees of frontier developers; large frontier developers must also provide an anonymous internal reporting process

Large frontier developers: civil penalties up to $1 million per violation (e.g. failing to publish or transmit required documents, failing to report an incident, or not complying with their own framework), recoverable only in a civil action by the Attorney General

timeline.note: Effective 1 January 2026: non-urgency statute enacted 29 September 2025, effective January 1 following a 90-day period from enactment under Cal. Const. art. IV, sec. 8(c)(1). Consistent with secondary reporting (WilmerHale).
